artists.name: Augustė Vickunaitė
artists.bio:
AUGUSTĖ VICKUNAITĖ has worked with reel-to-reel tape recorders since 2016 — playing them, recording to them, and letting the decay of the machines take part.

Found material, field recordings, voice, objects and the whole spectrum of the equipment's malfunctions are layered against each other: tape music and collage, theatrical, darkly funny, in no hurry. She has played Cafe OTO, KM28, the Volksbühne, Seanaps and Braille Satellite.

artists.name: Deeat Palace
artists.bio:
Brussels. Electronic and improvised music built largely on a Serge modular system — the first record, Pièces pour Serge, is two long pieces for that instrument alone.

Since then: s.canners on Prix Libre, releases on MIND Records and Erratum Musical, and a live practice that runs from trance-inducing repetition to something closer to folk.

artists.name: bivou4c
artists.bio:
A DJ from Paris, in Brussels — after strength in shared bass amplitudes, as they put it themselves.

Half of the label Bientôt Veuves, and a regular at Métaphore collectif nights between Paris and Marseille.

artists.name: Marc Matter
artists.bio:
Born in Basel in 1974, working in Düsseldorf. A founding member of Institut fuer Feinmotorik and, on his own, a maker of serial word compositions and sample-poetry — speech fragments lifted from news headlines and advertising, layered and repeated until they become material.

He studied at the Kunsthochschule für Medien in Cologne, has taught music and text at the IMM in Düsseldorf since 2010, and won the Karl Sczuka Prize for radio art in 2011 for Die 50 Skulpturen des Institut fuer Feinmotorik.

artists.name: Tresque
artists.bio:
TRESQUE is Laurent Peter, who also performs as d'incise and runs the INSUB. label — the name is taken from a half-forgotten medieval dance and put to work as an idea of techno.

The music is carved in circular movements out of samples and amplified noise, dub technique on one side and musique concrète on the other, grooves reduced to their shortest form and held between standing still and moving.

artists.name: De Kriekelaar
artists.bio: Gallaitstraat 86, 1030 Schaarbeek. A gemeenschapscentrum — a Flemish community centre in Brussels — running concerts, theatre, workshops and school programmes, and lending its rooms to whoever is doing something in the neighbourhood.

artists.name: Zohastre
artists.bio:
French-italian duo, whirlwind combination of spacio-tribal drums and bewitched electronics. Conjuring up harrowing medieval spirits & tripped out bag-pipe merriment with complex and repetitive rhythmic patterns, ethereal undulating sounds and guttural sub bass.

Like troubadours from outer space, ZOHASTRE venture into an hallucinated quest, ecstatic and psychedelic cavalcade, through the night, the forest, the universe. Practicing hypnotic audio gestures, they unleash impro-ritualistic music for trance-like FX.
